title: Count Connected Components in LCM Graph
summary: Given an array of integers nums of size n and a positive integer threshold, determine the number of connected components in a graph where nodes are connected if their least common multiple is less than or equal to the threshold.
statement: Given an array of integers nums of size n and a positive integer threshold, determine the number of connected components in a graph where nodes are connected if their least common multiple is less than or equal to the threshold. Each node's value corresponds to an element in nums. A connected component is a subgraph where every pair of vertices is connected by a path, and no vertex connects to a vertex outside the component.
constraints: nums has up to 100,000 distinct positive values; threshold is at most 200,000.
Two array positions share an undirected edge exactly when their least common multiple is at most threshold.
Return the number of connected components; every value above threshold is necessarily isolated.
hints: Values connect through any common multiple not exceeding the threshold.
Use multiples as virtual union-find nodes; all multiples of each present value join its component.
For each value at most threshold, union it with every bounded multiple, then count distinct roots plus large isolated values.
A direct LCM edge supplies a shared multiple, and chains through virtual multiples exactly preserve graph connectivity.
editorial: A direct LCM edge supplies a shared multiple, and chains through virtual multiples exactly preserve graph connectivity.

tests.explanation: Only values two and four connect; eight, three, and nine are isolated, giving four components.
Values two, three, four, eight, and nine connect through bounded common multiples; twelve is isolated.
